proposed_comments.title: Normalize persisted BeforePinned recent-item placement
proposed_comments.body:
### Normalize persisted BeforePinned recent-item placement

**Severity:** `high`

This PR hides the `Before pinned` option in both settings ComboBoxes, but existing settings files can still deserialize numeric value `1` into `RecentCommandsPlacement.BeforePinned`. Because `SettingsService.ApplyMigrations()` only normalizes pinned commands, those users keep the removed ordering mode after upgrade, so recent items can still appear before pinned items even though the UI no longer offers or explains that state. Please normalize both `RecentCommandsOnQuickAccessShelf` and `RecentCommandsOnHome` from `BeforePinned` to `AfterPinned` during settings load and save the migrated settings, with regression coverage.

confidence.rationale: The live head still has enum value BeforePinned = 1 and hidden UI choices, while SettingsService.ApplyMigrations only calls NormalizePinnedCommands. Persisted JSON value 1 therefore remains reachable after upgrade.

evidence: SettingsModel.cs lines 64 and 66 persist RecentCommandsPlacement values for the shelf and Home.
SettingsModel.cs line 561 keeps BeforePinned = 1 for deserialization compatibility.
SettingsService.cs lines 99-104 only normalize pinned commands during load migrations.
GeneralPage.xaml and AppearancePage.xaml hide the BeforePinned ComboBox item, making the state unavailable in the UI.

proposed_comments.title: Capitalize Home in the shelf teaching tip
proposed_comments.body:
### Capitalize Home in the shelf teaching tip

**Severity:** `low`

`Home` is used as the Command Palette page name elsewhere. Keeping it lowercase in the empty-shelf teaching tip makes the proper-noun UI label inconsistent with the surrounding settings text.

```suggestion
    <value>Pin a command to Home or adjust which pinned and recent items appear in Shelf settings. Empty shelves stay hidden.</value>
```

confidence.rationale: The current diff adds this resource string with lowercase home, while neighboring Command Palette UI text refers to Home as a page/surface name.
